verdicts.note: The Chinese-remainder-map page is the later page, since it applies its map to the coefficients of radix-digit convolution. It should not reuse p for a cyclic position, because p there is the coefficient index running over 0,...,2d-2. Use another letter (for example k) for the cyclic position, or say explicitly that p means a cyclic position here and not the coefficient index of the radix-digit page.

The Chinese-remainder-map page is the later page. There w is an output position with 0 <= w < T, while on the radix-digit page w is the digit width in bits (B = 2^w). The map page should use another letter for the output position (for example v), or say that w here is an output position and not the digit width.

The prime-source-lengths page is the later page, since it builds on the Chinese-remainder map (its s_a are the moduli of that map). There it says 'Let q denote a prime', but q on the Chinese-remainder-map page is a second cyclic position with 0 <= q < T. The prime-source-lengths page should write the prime with another letter (for example r is taken, so use something like pi or ell), or say that q here is a prime and not the cyclic position of the map page.
